question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, CFO Kress said gross margin bottoms at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 because of memory costs, then recovers to 72-73% in FY28. The Q3 guide was 74.0% ±50bp, with GAAP equal to non-GAAP. NVIDIA guides at a point ±50bp, usually in half-point steps, and has historically delivered on multi-quarter margin previews, so 71.5 is the mode and 71.0/72.0 come next. Memory prices 'headed even higher' and a possible 0.1-0.2pt GAAP discount tilt slightly low. Market check: the Polymarket brackets are for the Q3 actual non-GAAP margin, not the Q4 GAAP guide; they are a non-matching contract with about $140 volume and implausible prices, so I did not use them. No Kalshi or Manifold market on this metric. Live web tools failed this run, so evidence came from earlier logged research.

- Q3 FY27 outlook (same release): revenue $108.0B ±2%; GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% ±50bp; no China data-center compute assumed.
- Q1 FY27 (May 20, 2026): GAAP/non-GAAP GM 74.9%/75.0%; Q2 guide 74.9%/75.0% ±50bp.
- Q2 call (Aug 26, 2026; Webull/Benzinga/TIKR/The Elec/CNBC recaps): CFO Kress said GM bottoms in Q4 FY27 at 71%-72%, then settles at 72%-73% in FY28 as executed price increases take effect in Q1 FY28. Recaps do not say whether this was GAAP or non-GAAP.

- FY26 GAAP GM 71.1% vs non-GAAP 71.3%. GAAP/non-GAAP gap 0.0-0.1pt in FY27 so far.
- Guide format: a point ±50bp, usually at 0.5pt steps (73.5, 74.0, 75.0) but sometimes odd tenths (e.g. GAAP 71.8 vs non-GAAP 72.0 historically; 74.9 in Q2 FY27).
- Preview precedent: FY26 'mid-70s exit' preview was followed by a Q4 FY26 guide of ~75.0%.
- Status quo: the Q4 GAAP GM guide follows management's stated 71-72% trough range.
- Resolves off the GAAP gross margin figure in the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (expected ~Nov 18-19, 2026), not non-GAAP and not the actual Q3 or Q4 result.
- Event window: Q3 FY27 earnings release (criteria text blank; scheduled resolution 2026-11-17); as of 2026-10-15 the guide has not been issued.
- Market note: the Polymarket brackets found are for the Q3 actual adjusted (non-GAAP) GM, a different contract, and thinly traded.
- Searched but not found (this and earlier runs): any post-August management update on Q4 GM, consensus Q4 GM estimates, the full call transcript, and any market on the Q4 GM guide itself.

- Q2 FY27 (reported Aug 2026): revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), data center $89.0B; GAAP gross margin 75.0% vs 72.4% a year earlier, attributed to Blackwell Ultra mix (CoinPaper, 2026-10-14).

- R&D rose ~64% y/y to $7.05B per quarter; supply commitments $279B; management says China data center compute is limited by export restrictions (AOL, 2026-10-14).
- Status quo: next-quarter GAAP GM guidance has sat in the mid-70s through FY27. The Q4 FY27 guide comes in the Q3 FY27 release, scheduled around 2026-11-17 to 18.
- Historical comparison: during the Blackwell ramp (FY25 Q4 to FY26 Q1), GAAP GM guidance fell to ~70.6-71% before recovering to the mid-70s. A Rubin ramp in late CY2026 is the main candidate for a similar dip. On the other side, mix and pricing kept margins at or above 74-75% through FY27.
- One-off charges (e.g., the FY26 Q1 H20 inventory charge that took GAAP GM to ~60.5%) were reported in actuals, not built into forward guidance.
- Base rate: NVIDIA's quarter-to-quarter change in next-quarter GAAP GM guidance usually stays within about +/-1.5pp outside product-transition periods; transition quarters have seen moves of ~3-4pp.

calls.reconciliation: Core dispute: whether management already foreshadowed a 71-72% Q4 FY27 GM trough. Runs 1-2 cite it from multiple independent recaps; Run 3 did not have this evidence and anchored on a mid-70s status quo (p_above_upper 0.5). I attempted 2 web searches and 1 fetch to verify the CFO quote and the Q3 74.0% GAAP guide; all three failed with API errors, so nothing was independently retrieved. I accept the Runs 1-2 premise because it is attested by many named, distinct outlets and is consistent with the question's range (68.95-73.05, centered ~71), which was likely set around expected guidance. Run 3's view is thus a factual gap, not a judgment I weigh equally. Carried forward Runs 1-2 reference class; dispersion set slightly wider than Run 1 for residual memory-cost and GAAP-adjustment uncertainty. Small upside escape priced for the case the recaps misstated the trough or price increases offset memory.
